chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all of them from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The prescribed penalty (hadd) of flogging applies when two people are found in one bed covering. So the two men shall be flogged the hadd punishment when they are apprehended in one bed covering, and the two women shall be flogged the hadd punishment when they are apprehended in one bed covering.

key_terms.الْجَلْد: jald — flogging, the specific form of corporal punishment prescribed here
key_terms.الْحَدّ: hadd — the divinely prescribed punishment for specific offenses enumerated in Islamic law, as distinct from ta'zir (discretionary punishment)
key_terms.لِحَاف: lihaf — a bed covering or quilt; the physical circumstance that triggers this ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for two people found in the same bed covering according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the hadd penalty of flogging is triggered by the outward circumstance of two persons of the same sex being found sharing a single bed covering. This ruling, from the chapter on what necessitates flogging (Chapter 5 of Kitab al-Hudud in al-Kafi), addresses a case short of intercourse — mere co-occupation of a bed covering by two men or two women constitutes grounds for the prescribed corporal punishment. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, jurists debated whether this ruling presupposed suspicion of an indecent act or applied automatically upon discovery; this hadith from the reliable chain through al-Halabi is among the primary evidences cited in the discussion.
